hierarchy-morphs.visual_critic_note: Clean card chrome and intentional muted palette lift it above defaults, but the circle pack is clipped at the bottom of the viewport — a layout bug that prevents the full hierarchy from being seen — and the cryptic synthetic labels (s0, g2, root) add noise without communicating anything to a viewer.
hierarchy-morphs.encoding_integrity_note: Encoding is structurally honest — scaleSqrt for force radii, D3 pack/treemap/partition all use area-correct algorithms, key functions on node/label joins — but connection paths key on array index instead of a stable ID, making them vulnerable to permutation-relation failure on data shuffles.
hierarchy-morphs.stress_test_note: Interaction robustness is strong—RAF coalescing on the bundling slider, dirty-flag loop for force simulation, and .interrupt() guards before every layout transition—but force-mode drag registers no touch event filtering, leaving mousedown/touchstart open to double-trigger on mobile.
hierarchy-morphs.cognitive_load_note: Single-view-at-a-time design keeps working memory load low and the 7-color palette is perceptually separable in the circle pack, but simultaneously animating 200+ nodes across radically different layout topologies (pack→force, pack→sunburst) risks motion chaos that cannot be assessed from a static screenshot, and the 300 bundled leaf connections would likely become a hairball if opacity or bundling were relaxed.
